outline.chapter_title: Introduction: The State of Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs
outline.description: This chapter introduces the challenges of mathematical reasoning for language models, reviews the landscape of existing open-source and closed-source models, and presents the core contributions of DeepSeekMath. It sets the stage by defining the gap between current open models and state-of-the-art proprietary systems.
subtopics: The Complexity of Mathematical Reasoning in AI
Limitations of Current Open-Source Models vs. GPT-4/Gemini-Ultra
Overview of DeepSeekMath: Goals and Achievements
Key Contributions: Scalable Pre-training and Efficient Reinforcement Learning
Benchmark Landscape: GSM8K, MATH, and Formal Proofs

outline.chapter_title: Constructing the DeepSeekMath Corpus: Data Engineering at Scale
outline.description: This chapter details the methodology behind creating the 120B token DeepSeekMath Corpus. It covers the iterative pipeline for mining high-quality mathematical data from Common Crawl, the use of classifiers for data selection, and strategies for decontamination and multilingual inclusion.
subtopics: The Potential of Web Data vs. Academic Papers (ArXiv)
Iterative Data Selection Pipeline using fastText Classifiers
Seed Corpus Initialization and Negative Sampling
Domain-Based Expansion and Human Annotation Loops
Decontamination Strategies to Prevent Benchmark Leakage
Multilingual Considerations: English and Chinese Data Integration

outline.chapter_title: Pre-Training Strategy: From Code to Mathematics
outline.description: This chapter explores the pre-training philosophy behind DeepSeekMath-Base. It analyzes the decision to initialize with a code-trained model, investigates the synergy between code and math training, and evaluates the efficacy of different data mixtures compared to traditional academic corpora.
subtopics: Initialization Choice: Why Start with DeepSeek-Coder?
Experimental Analysis: Code Training as a Catalyst for Reasoning
Two-Stage vs. One-Stage Training Regimes
The Surprising Inefficacy of ArXiv Papers in Isolation
Data Mixture Composition: Balancing Math, Code, and Natural Language
Performance Validation: DeepSeekMath-Base vs. Minerva and Llemma

outline.description: This chapter describes the transition from a base model to an instruction-tuned model. It outlines the curation of diverse solution formats (Chain-of-Thought, Program-of-Thought, Tool-Integrated) and evaluates the resulting DeepSeekMath-Instruct model against contemporary competitors.
subtopics: Curating High-Quality Instruction Tuning Data
Solution Formats: CoT, PoT, and Tool-Integrated Reasoning
Training Hyperparameters and Context Management
Evaluation Protocol: Tool-Free vs. Tool-Assisted Solving
Comparative Analysis Against 7B to 70B Open-Source Models
Performance Gaps Relative to Proprietary Models (GPT-4, Gemini)
